issue_context.body:
### Summary

I'm using ansible from archlinux packages, version 5.0.1, ansible-core 2.12.0-1.

The lookup 'first_found' doesn't find any files at all.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

first_found.py

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

  config file = /home/hawara/whg/infra-ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/hawara/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /home/hawara/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.9.9 (main, Nov 20 2021, 21:30:06) [GCC 11.1.0]
  jinja version = 3.0.3
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed

```


### OS / Environment

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
Example playbook: test.yml
```yaml (paste below)
---
- hosts: localhost
  tasks:
  - name: test lookup
    debug:
      msg: "{{ query('first_found', files=['rasdaemon.yml', 'default.yml', 'q'], paths=[ '/tmp/zh', '/tmp' ], errors='ignore') }}"
```

### Actual Results

comments:
Files identified in the description:
* [`lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py)

If these files are incorrect, please update the `component name` section of the description or use the `!component` bot command.

[click here for bot help](https://github.com/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/devel/ISSUE_HELP.md)
<!--- boilerplate: components_banner --->

It appears that according to the [docs](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/first_found_lookup.html) (and code) your example is not supposed to work:
> This lookup can be used in ‘dual mode’, either passing a list of file names or a dictionary that has files and paths.


Use the following instead:
```yaml

- debug:
    msg: "{{ query('first_found', params, errors='ignore') }}"
  vars:
    params:
      files:
        - 'rasdaemon.yml'
        - 'default.yml'
        - 'q'
      paths:
        - '/tmp/zh'
        - '/tmp'
```

Then there is also:
> Either a list of files _terms or a key files with a list of files is required for this plugin to operate.

but this does not work (example from docs):
```yaml
- debug:
    msg: "{{ query('first_found', files=file_list, errors='ignore') }}"
  vars:
    file_list:
      - /tmp/zh/rasdaemon.yml
      - /tmp/zh/default.yml
```

while this does work:
```yaml
- debug:
    msg: "{{ query('first_found', file_list, errors='ignore') }}"
  vars:
    file_list:
      - /tmp/zh/rasdaemon.yml
      - /tmp/zh/default.yml
```

and this does not work either (example from docs):
```yaml
- debug:
    msg: "{{ query('first_found', file_list, paths=['/tmp/zh'],  errors='ignore') }}"
  vars:
    file_list:
      - 'rasdaemon.yml'
      - 'default.yml'
```

So there seems to be contradiction between docs and what the code actually does. So either some of the examples in the documentation or the code needs to be fixed.
its a bug, it should handle this case also, the old 'params' is what we are moving away from

probably not this simple, but this should be the fix:

```diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py
index 5d54959ec5..a664c5b7ba 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py

+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/lookup/first_found.py
@@ -166,6 +166,9 @@ class LookupModule(LookupBase):
         total_search = []
         skip = False

+        if not terms:
+            terms = self.get_option('files')
+
         # can use a dict instead of list item to pass inline config
         for term in terms:
             if isinstance(term, Mapping):```

review_comments:
There's a TODO below which fixes some of the test breakage:

```python
                # NOTE: this seems wrong, should be 'extend' as any option/entry can clobber all
                total_search = filelist
```

This fixes it
```diff
-                total_search = filelist
+                total_search.extend(filelist)
```
